LESSON: READING 9.2.1 READING COMPREHENSION: POETRY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we describe a poem?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify components of a poem for comprehension
2. read poems based on the theme for comprehension
3. answer questions from a poem based on the theme
4. appreciate reading poems for personal judgement

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 9.2.1 READING COMPREHENSION: POETRY
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 9.2.1 READING COMPREHENSION: POETRY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify components of a poem for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to identify components of a poem for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify components of a poem for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify components of a poem for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Read poems based on the theme for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to read poems based on the theme for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read poems based on the theme for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read poems based on the theme for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Answer questions from a poem based on the theme

What this means
In this part you learn to answer questions from a poem based on the theme. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: answer questions from a poem based on the theme.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can answer questions from a poem based on the theme. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate reading poems for personal judgement

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate reading poems for personal judgement. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate reading poems for personal judgement.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate reading poems for personal judgement. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify components of a poem for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry to a partner. (skill: read poems based on the theme for comprehension)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: answer questions from a poem based on the theme)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: appreciate reading poems for personal judgement)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify components of a poem for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: read poems based on the theme for comprehension.
4. Practise this skill: answer questions from a poem based on the theme.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we describe a poem?
2. Why do we read poems?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 9.2.1 Reading Comprehension: Poetry means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify components of a poem for comprehension.
5. Be able to: read poems based on the theme for comprehension.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
